overview: Apple posted fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $109.4B, up 16% YoY, led by iPhone (+22%) and Mac (+29%), while Services slowed to 12% from 16%. Kevan Parekh, CFO, guided September-quarter growth to 9%-11%, citing FX and worsening advanced-node SoC supply constraints, and memory costs more than explained the gross margin decline.
keyTakeaways: Tim Cook, CEO, blamed SoC supply constraints on a demand forecast miss and said Apple will be "scrambling" on supply this quarter.
Parekh said a ~2.5 point FX headwind plus a significant sequential rise in supply constraints explain the ~500bp guided deceleration.
Cook said Apple "reluctantly" raised iPad and Mac prices on memory costs and that it is too early to judge elasticity.
Siri AI cannot yet launch on EU iPhone and iPad, and China has approved only original Apple Intelligence features, per Cook.
financialHighlights: Revenue was $109.4B (+16%), with Products $78.7B (+18%), Services $30.7B (+12%) and iPad down 6% to $6.2B.
Gross margin was 50.1% including a ~2 point tariff refund benefit, or 48.1% ex-refund versus 49.3% in March.
Diluted EPS rose 29% to $2.02, including $0.11 from tariff refunds, while operating expenses rose 23% to $19.1B on R&D.
Operating cash flow was $34.4B and shareholder returns were $33B, including $25.8B of buybacks.
guidance: Kevan Parekh, CFO, guided September-quarter revenue growth of 9%-11%, with iPhone up mid-teens, and gave nothing beyond September.
Parekh expects Services growth similar to June's 12% after removing a ~2.5 point negative FX impact.
Parekh guided gross margin of 47%-48% including ~1 point of tariff refunds (46.5% ex-refund), opex of $19.1B-$19.4B and a ~16.5% tax rate.
Tim Cook, CEO, expects memory costs to rise further in September, with the carry-in inventory offset shrinking afterward.

qa.question: How much do supply constraints hit the December quarter, and could Apple broaden silicon suppliers?
qa.answer: Cook said the cause is a demand forecast miss, not a supplier issue, citing over 100 million components from Arizona this year; Kevan Parekh, CFO, gave no color beyond September.
qa.read: Declined to quantify; pushed back on the supplier premise.

qa.question: Does pricing protect gross profit dollars or margin, and why did Services slow to 12%?
qa.answer: Parekh named FX as the main driver, plus the year-ago F1 release, mobile gaming softness and the U.S. link-out ruling, with FX a ~5 point Services headwind from March to September; Tim Cook, CEO, said pricing weighs units, revenue and margin long term.

qa.question: What drives the gross margin walk to the ~46.5% ex-refund midpoint, and where is Siri AI in China and Europe?
qa.answer: Parekh said memory more than explains both the 120bp fall to 48.1% and the 160bp step to 46.5%, with FX minimal; Tim Cook, CEO, said Siri AI is or will be on Mac in the EU but not iPhone or iPad.

qa.question: Has demand been pulled forward ahead of memory-driven price increases?
qa.answer: Cook said pull-forward is not obvious given iPhone's 22% year-to-date growth, and elasticity on iPad and Mac price increases will be clearer in the weeks ahead.

unanswered.question: The December-quarter impact of supply constraints.
unanswered.how: Kevan Parekh, CFO, said Apple is "not providing any color" beyond September.

unanswered.question: Siri AI capital intensity and competition from OpenAI or SpaceX AI devices.
unanswered.how: Tim Cook, CEO, called the cost balance uncertain; John Ternus, Incoming CEO, did not comment on competitors.

unanswered.question: Apple Upgrade adoption and its effect on replacement cycles.
unanswered.how: Tim Cook, CEO, said uptake remains to be seen, with no figures.
